newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvests 52 pct of crops vs 60 avg.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvests 52 pct of crops vs 60 avg.

text.p: Saskatchewan had harvested 52 percent of all crops in the week ended September 23 compared with 60 percent for the period in the five-year average, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its report.

Grade quality was above average for harvest spring wheat despite recent rains which reduced crop quality across the grainbelt. With 49 percent of spring wheat havested, 80 percent was expected to grade number one, 16 percent grading number two, four percent grading number three.
The 10-year average for spring wheat was 47 percent at No1, 24 percent at No2, 19 percent at No3 and 10 percent feed.
Rain and wind were the most frequently reported causes of crop damage in the past week, followed by frost.
Southern Saskatchewan saw an average one mm of rain. There was frost damage near Weyburn, Regina, Maple Creek and Leader.

Central Saskatchewan saw an average 21 mm of rain. Rain caused flooding, bleaching and sprouting in many central areas. There was frost damage around Canora, Saskatoon, Kindersley and Biggar. Ergot was reported in wheat near Melville, while smut was reported in wheat near Watrous.
Northern Saskatchewan saw an average 20 mm of rain. Rain caused bleaching and sprouting.
Humboldt and Meadown Lake reported frost.
